title: Fresh contradictory QA after bounded transient sourceId repair

evidence: user:private-course is rejected by transient admission before source-byte read
dot/dash/underscore identity crosses transient admission and M3.3 prepare/verify
0/161/254/255/256/300/512 character probes cannot yield transient PASS

finding.title: Case-distinct transient sourceIds can collide during mandatory M3.3 local materialization on case-insensitive filesystems
finding.cause: Transient admission and exact-string binding allow distinct sourceIds such as CourseA and coursea. M3.3 derives local temporary filenames <sourceId>.source for every resource, writes all sources, then rebuilds FactoryContext from those paths. On a case-insensitive Windows filesystem those two paths alias, so distinct admitted exact source bytes cannot both remain independently materialized.
finding.contractImpact: Issue #348 requires every transient-PASS sourceId to be safely materializable by M3.3 under the supported local processing model. A multi-source pair that is individually valid but aliases after M3.3 filename derivation violates that invariant.
reproduction: Both CourseA and coursea satisfy transient.SOURCE_ID and independently produce PASS_TRANSIENT_SOURCE_ADMISSION_V1 for different exact bytes
PureWindowsPath('CourseA.source') equals PureWindowsPath('coursea.source') under Windows path semantics
Windows CI executes actual M3.3 prepare/verify with both IDs and distinct exact source bytes
